newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DSF wants to attract more male viewers.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DSF wants to attract more male viewers.

text.p: German television sports network DSF said on Tuesday it would intensify efforts to target the 14-49 age group for male viewers and expected a 25 percent increase in 1997 advertising net sales.
DSF managing director Rainer Huether said the network would introduce new programming and production, as well as new presenters, in mid-February in a bid to boost male viewership.
Huether said the targeted age group attracts about one-third of all advertising expenditures in Germany and that the male target group was a "growth market for the future".
DSF's viewership is about 70 percent male, the highest male portion in Germany, he said.

DSF net advertising sales in 1995 were about 70 million marks and rose to about 100 million marks in 1996. Huether said DSF expected advertising growth in 1997 of about 25 percent and that the network would turn a profit in about five years.

He refused to comment on reports that the network had a 1996 loss of about 120 million marks. But he said losses compared with 1995 were "clearly less" and said television required long-term investments.
DSF is owned by Munich media mogul Leo Kirch, who holds a direct 49.4 percent stake in the network and another 24.9 percent stake through Taurus GmbH, which is owned by Kirch's media group.
